title: fledge.yml
description: What a project tells Fledge about its app: how it presents itself to the person who runs it. Every key is optional, and an unknown key fails the build.

name.description: The app's name (default: the gemspec's name, or the project folder's name, camelized). It may have spaces.

kind.description: console (default), an app that runs in a terminal, or windowed, one that opens its own windows.

identifier.description: The app's reverse-DNS name, such as com.example.MyCoolApp, which macOS and Windows know it by, and the bundle identifier or applicationId of a phone's app (needed when windowed, and for a phone): letters, digits, and hyphens, in two or more parts between dots, in at most 128 characters.

version.description: The app's version, such as "1.2.3" (default: the gemspec's, or 0.0.0): a version RubyGems reads that begins with a number. Quote it, since YAML reads 1.10 as the number 1.1.

icon.description: The icon's files without their extension, relative to the project's root, such as icons/app: icons/app.icns on macOS, icons/app.ico on Windows (16 to 256 pixels), icons/app-16.png, -32, -64, -128, -256, and -512 on Linux (those there are, at least one), icons/app-1024.png for iOS, and icons/app-48.png, -72, -96, -144, and -192 for Android.

publisher.description: Who makes the app (default: the gemspec's authors).

copyright.description: The app's copyright notice, such as "© 2026 Example, Inc." (default: none).

description.description: One line that says what the app does, such as Keeps your notes (default: none): a Linux desktop entry's Comment, a .deb's synopsis, and a Windows program's Comments.

long_description.description: More about the app, in paragraphs (default: none): a .deb's extended description, after the description.

homepage.description: The app's web page, an http or https URL, such as https://example.com/cool-app (default: none): a .deb's Homepage, and the links of a Windows setup program's entry in Settings.

license_file.description: The app's license text, a UTF-8 file in the project, such as LICENSE.txt (default: none): a Windows setup program shows it on a page before it installs, and a .deb installs it as /usr/share/doc/PACKAGE/copyright.

installers.description: Which of dmg, nsis, appimage, deb, and msix a windowed app gets, such as [dmg] or [] for none (default: dmg, nsis, and appimage). An msix needs windows: msix_publisher. A console app gets none.

programs.description: The programs the project ships in one folder, sharing one runtime, one copy of the project, and one set of gems, such as a windowed game and its command line (default: the one program you build). Each has a path, and a name, kind, identifier, and icon of its own; at most one is windowed, and no two share a name or an identifier. With programs, kind, identifier, and icon belong to each program, and name, version, publisher, copyright, and installers to the project.

path.description: The program's file, relative to the project's root, with / between folders, such as bin/cli or gui/main.rb.

name.description: The program's name, its file's name in the built folder, and what people see (default: for a console program, its path's file name without the extension, such as cli for bin/cli; for a windowed one, the project's name).

kind.description: console (default), a program that runs in a terminal, or windowed, one that opens its own windows and gets the project's installers.

ios.description: What fledge build ios lays over the Xcode project it writes (default: nothing). Desktop builds ignore it.

host.description: A folder in the project, such as host/ios, whose files fledge build ios copies over the project before XcodeGen reads it: each replaces Fledge's file at the same path, such as Host/main.m, Host/Info.plist, or project.yml, or joins the project. Fledge fills its @@NAME@@ marks in a copy of project.yml.

android.description: What fledge build android lays over the Gradle project it writes (default: nothing). Desktop builds ignore it.

host.description: A folder in the project, such as host/android, whose files fledge build android copies over the project: each replaces Fledge's file at the same path, such as src/main/java/org/setdef/fledge/host/MainActivity.java, or joins the project. Fledge fills its @@NAME@@ marks in a copy of one of its Gradle files, the manifest, strings.xml, or MainActivity.java.

linux.description: What a build for Linux needs to know of the computers the app goes to (default: nothing). Other builds ignore it.

system_libraries.description: The libraries the project's gems load from the Linux distribution, by the names their compiled files give them, such as [libwebkit2gtk-4.1.so.0, libgtk-3.so.0] (default: none). fledge build accepts a gem that needs one, refuses one that no gem's compiled file needs from the system, and makes a .deb depend on the packages that provide them; the app says which is missing on a computer that lacks one.

deb_changelog.description: The app's changelog, a file in the project, such as CHANGELOG.md (default: none), which a .deb installs compressed as /usr/share/doc/PACKAGE/changelog.gz.

macos.description: What a build for macOS writes in place of what it derives (default: nothing). Other builds ignore it.

build.description: The app's build number, its Info.plist's CFBundleVersion, which the App Store and updaters compare: one to three whole numbers between periods, such as "42" or "1.2.417", quoted (default: the version's first three numbers, as CFBundleShortVersionString).

windows.description: The package identity of a Windows app's MSIX package, which an msix installer needs (default: nothing). Other builds ignore it.

msix_name.description: The package's name, Partner Center's Package/Identity/Name for an app in the Microsoft Store: 3 to 50 letters, digits, periods, and hyphens (default: the identifier).

msix_publisher.description: The package's publisher, a distinguished name, such as CN=Example: Partner Center's Package/Identity/Publisher for the Microsoft Store, which signs the package, or the subject of the certificate you sign it with.

file_associations.description: The files and folders a windowed app opens, in Tauri's and electron-builder's terms (default: none). macOS lists them as the bundle's document types, ranked Alternate, so the app is offered and never made the default; Windows' setup program adds the app to Open with for each extension, and to the menu of every folder for folders; a Linux desktop entry lists their MIME types, and inode/directory for folders, and passes the paths as arguments. A file or folder dropped on a Windows program arrives in ARGV; on macOS it arrives as an Apple event, which only a GUI library's event loop receives. Only a windowed app has them.

name.description: What a person calls these documents, such as Project archive, which each system shows as their kind.

role.description: viewer (default), an app that reads them, or editor, one that also writes them: macOS's CFBundleTypeRole.

extensions.description: The files' extensions, without the dot, such as [zip], which macOS and Windows know a file by.

mime_types.description: The files' MIME types, such as [application/zip], which a Linux desktop knows a file by.

content_types.description: The files' uniform type identifiers on macOS, such as [public.zip-archive]; given, macOS goes by them and not by extensions or MIME types.

folders.description: true for an entry that opens folders, and names no files (default: false).

build_tools.description: true to put in the app the tools fledge build --from runs that a system lacks, so that the app, with Fledge in its Gemfile as an ordinary gem, builds an app from itself on a computer with no Ruby and no runtime (default: false): on Windows the runtime's launchers, rcedit, and NSIS, and on Linux the AppImage runtime, in its tools folder; on macOS nothing, since macOS has its tools. An app fledge build --from writes keeps them only when its own fledge.yml sets build_tools.
